hypotheses.title: Idiosyncratic Risk Spike Normalization (model51)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Stocks experiencing temporary surges in 30-day unsystematic variance relative to their 360-day baseline (unsystematic_risk_last_30_days / unsystematic_risk_last_360_days) suffer from transient liquidity panics or event overreactions. As market conditions normalize, idiosyncratic risk contracts, producing steady excess risk-adjusted returns with low turnover and zero self-correlation.
confounders: Permanent operational impairment or catastrophic fraud altering baseline variance permanently
Protracted litigation creating ongoing binary outcomes
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during high-volatility financial crises where idiosyncratic distress triggers widespread defaults.

hypotheses.title: Subindustry Defensive Low-Beta Anomaly (model51)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical asset pricing confirms that retail leverage constraints and institutional tracking error mandates systematically inflate high-beta asset valuations. Within each subindustry, selecting securities with the lowest 60-day regression beta relative to SPY (-beta_last_60_days_spy) isolates steady, capital-preserving compounders that deliver superior risk-adjusted returns with minimal maximum drawdown.
confounders: Sudden speculative momentum surges where low-quality high-beta junk leads the market
Beta compression caused by severe trading illiquidity
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during aggressive early-stage market cyclical recoveries characterized by high-beta speculative rallies.

hypotheses.title: Volatility-Scaled Statistical Price Reversion (pv1)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Dividing the 5-day price displacement by the 20-day historical standard deviation of close prices (ts_std_dev(close, 20)) converts raw dollar changes into a statistical z-score. Ranking the negative z-score within each subindustry buys temporarily oversold equities while dampening turnover and avoiding price-level distortions.
confounders: Fundamental structural repricing driven by earnings revisions or major news events
Protracted momentum trend continuation in high-volatility stocks
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during strong momentum trends where overextended equities continue trending without reverting.
